**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ -  Net long positioning in Comex gold declined by almost 3.6 million ounces, with fresh short positions accounting for more than 60% of this change. Net longs now languish at their lowest level since December 2008. -  Gold ETF flows in the week to May 11th paint a slightly less bleak picture of investment demand. Led by solid additions to three of the largest funds we monitor, overall holdings increased by nearly 94,000 ounces. The inflows were offset by some light selling from smaller funds.  Net long speculative positions in Comex silver were slashed aggressively in the week to May 8th. A significant entry of fresh shorts accounted for a large portion of the 31 million ounce change—the biggest intraweek shortening since mid-November 2012. Clearly there is a shared feeling among the speculative community that silver could have some room to go lower before we begin to see a reversal. -  Silver ETF’s shed a sizable 3.9 million ounces of their holdings last week. The iShares fund - by far the largest—accounted for nearly all of this selling. Last week’s net inflows to silver ETF’s, which broke a long pattern of weekly net sales, were clearly a blip in a larger trend that looks set to reassert itself as investor bearishness grows. -  Platinum futures positioning on Nymex resumed its bearish trend last week after a brief increase in net longs the week before. In the week to May 8th, fresh shorts entered the market to squeeze net long positioning by almost 100,000 ounces. At just below 900,000 ounces, this is the lowest net long positioning in platinum seen since August 2010. -  Palladium ETFs yet again saw net inflows last week, the bulk of which were to the largest fund by holdings. The market’s focus turned squarely back on to Europe after the elections in France and Greece on May 5th-6th. The victory for Franзois Hollande’s socialists in France and the failure of any Greek party to gain a controlling majority were widely interpreted as a sign of growing public discontentment with the austerity measures implemented across the Eurozone in the wake of several sovereign bailouts. This sparked fears that the painstaking progress made in recent months towards solving the region’s economic problems could be undone, and this was enough to shatter the fragile bullishness that had been steadily accumulating in the market. The selloff began on Tuesday the 8th after London returned after its Monday bank holiday. The usual victims—equities, the Euro, industrial metals—were all pushed lower and gold followed, in a move that further cements its current departure from the kind of safe-haven role we have seen it play during risk-off moves in recent memory. Having begun the week at $1,640, by Friday gold dipped as low as $1,572, recovering only slightly to finish the week at $1,580. -  Speculator bearishness in gold is plain to see from the slew of red figures in the table at the top of this page. -  Silver followed gold lower last week, dipping below $28.50 on Friday before recovering to close at $28.80, locking in a $1.35 loss on the week. Silver has now lost a hefty 9.2% since the beginning of May, making it the second-poorest performing of the precious metals in percentage terms this month after palladium. Each time silver has traded through a new round-dollar level this month (first $31, then $30, then $29) there has been a sense that _this_ may be the price beneath which the industrial demand that has been so lamentable this year may finally pick up. Deman

d did improve a little after last week’s move below $30 but, fearing that silver may have yet more downside to come, many buyers seem happy to wait patiently until the price moves even lower. -  Net long speculative positions in Comex silver were slashed aggressively in the week to May 8th. A significant entry of fresh shorts accounted for a large portion of the 31 million ounce change—the biggest intraweek shortening since mid-November 2012. Clearly there is a shared feeling among the speculative community that silver could have some room to go lower before we begin to see a reversal. -  Silver ETF’s shed a sizable 3.9 million ounces of their holdings last week. The iShares fund - by far the largest—accounted for nearly all of this selling. -  Platinum followed gold’s lead in the wake of last week’s European elections but, partly due to its stronger positive correlation with general economic growth expectations and partly due to an already poor technical outlook, platinum was hit that much harder than the yellow metal. Platinum lost around $70 on the week compared with go

ld’s $60 (or –4.7% compared with –3.6%). The move down through $1,500—anticipated by some as a potential short-term base—shifted the technical outlook from bad to worse. Friday’s low just above $1,460 marked a loss of nearly $120 since the beginning of the month. Buying interest has not been entirely absent—especially below $1,500 there was a notable uptick in industrial demand— but the torrent of investor selling thus far has been too strong for platinum to find any real foothold. -  Platinum futures positioning on Nymex resumed its bearish trend last week after a brief increase in net longs the week before. In the week to May 8th, fresh shorts entered the market to squeeze net long positioning by almost 100,000 ounces. At just below 900,000 ounces, this is the lowest net long positioning in platinum seen since August 2010. Interestingly, the ratio of net spec long gold positioning to net spec long platinum positioning has moved against platinum in recent weeks after several month’s gradual appreciation in platinum’s favour, underlining the bearish investor sentiment towards platinum at the moment. -  Platinum ETF’s were small net sellers for yet another week, shedding 3,600 ounces on the whole. While the size has been consistently modest, it remains a concern that the selling has persisted in spite of the significant drop in spot prices. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **14 May 2012** ## **Palladium CFTC data to 8 May 2012; ETF data to 11 May 2012.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

-  Palladium last week extended the rout that has seen it give up more than $80 since the beginning of May. This loss—equal to nearly 12.5% - marks palladium out as easily the weakest performer of the precious complex so far this month. (Silver is next closest with a loss of 9.2%.) Palladium was his especially hard on Tuesday the 8th, losing around $30—almost as much as gold and platinum lost, and obviously far more significant as a percentage. On Friday we saw $600 tested several times but this level held firm on the day. Psychologically it’s a big one and, coupled with the ever strengthening auto and industrial demand we witnessed as the price neared $600, could help prices to form a base around here in the coming weeks. -  In this report last week we cautioned that the steady accumulation of net long positioning seen in the previous few weeks could be susceptible to a reversal given the continued price weakness. Sure enough, in the week to May 8th longs scaled back their Nymex positions and some fresh shorts entered in size, making for a net shortening of 250,000 ounces. Net longs are now back to their lowest since January and the speculative friendliness that helped drive palladium higher through April appears to have fizzled out for the time being. However, with many people seeing $600 as a decent support zone for the time being, new shorts could find themselves easily squeezed if spot rallies from here. -  Palladium ETFs yet again saw net inflows last week, the bulk of which were to the largest fund by holdings.
